tools.name: provision_api_key
tools.description: CALL THIS FIRST. Provisions an API key for the operator. Returns a pcc_live_* key that must be included as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' on all subsequent requests. Accepts either email OR walletAddress. The key is shown once — save it. Without it, all other endpoints return 401.

email.description: Operator email address (use this OR walletAddress)

walletAddress.description: EVM wallet address (use this OR email)

capability.description: What the operator does — e.g. 'FDM 3D printing', 'CNC milling', 'HPLC analysis'

tools.name: list_api_keys
tools.description: List all active API keys for the authenticated operator. Returns key IDs, prefixes, scopes, rate limits, usage counts, and creation/expiry timestamps. Requires a valid API key or SIWE session.

tools.name: revoke_api_key
tools.description: Revoke an API key permanently. The key will immediately stop working. You must own the key. Use list_api_keys to find the key ID.

tools.name: setup_detect
tools.description: Auto-detect current setup state: env vars, database, adapters, chain connectivity, storage, identity. Use this to see what's configured and what's missing before onboarding.

tools.name: setup_generate_config
tools.description: Generate a KERNEL_CONFIG JSON from device descriptions. Tell it what machines you have and it produces the config ready to paste into your environment.

devices.description: Array of device descriptions with type, model, and connection info

tools.name: setup_validate
tools.description: Validate a kernel config (20+ checks: JSON structure, device connectivity, adapter compatibility). Returns validation errors and warnings.

tools.name: setup_register_device
tools.description: Register a device in the database with adapter config and capabilities. Part of Step 3 in the onboarding flow. Required: kernelId, deviceId, type and adapterType (400 missing_required_fields otherwise).

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to register the device under

deviceId.description: Your ID for this device, unique within the kernel

type.description: Device role: machine, sensor or camera (the values setup_generate_config and setup_validate accept)

model.description: Device model identifier (optional; stored as "unknown" if absent)

adapterType.description: One of octoprint, modbus, opcua, sila, ipp, generic-http or mock; the route refuses anything else (including opentrons)

tools.name: setup_test_job
tools.description: Submit a test job for one device on a kernel (Step 4 of onboarding). The gateway runs it only for a kernel it operates in-process; for any other kernel it refuses and runs nothing. Every reply says whether the job ran and passed.

tools.name: setup_status
tools.description: Comprehensive setup status across 6 categories: gateway, database, adapters, chain, storage, identity. Use to confirm everything is green before going live.

tools.name: list_capability_types
tools.description: List all capability types registered on the network (FDM, SLA, CNC, HPLC, etc.) with metadata.

tools.name: search_capabilities
tools.description: List the built-in capability type templates: each type's name, version, description, parameter count, parameter group names and a base price hint. NOTE: these describe types, not operators' offerings, and carry no assurance tiers or availability. The gateway does not read the query, so it never narrows the list. Registered capabilities of a type are listed by GET /api/capabilities?type=<type>.

query.description: Optional and not used: the gateway returns the full list whatever you send.

tools.name: get_build_options
tools.description: Get configuration options for a capability type: parameter groups, each parameter's definition, and a base price hint. It includes no assurance tiers. Use before calling calculate_price.

selections.description: Current selections to refine available options

tools.name: calculate_price
tools.description: Calculate price for a capability configuration. Returns base price, tier premiums, and estimated total cost.

tools.name: build_contract
tools.description: Build and submit a capability contract with on-chain milestone escrow. Returns job ID and escrow address.

tools.name: list_kernels
tools.description: List all Shop Kernels on the network with status and capability types. Optionally filter by status.

status.description: Filter by kernel status (online, offline, maintenance)

tools.name: get_kernel
tools.description: Get kernel details including full capability objects, devices, and queue.

tools.name: get_kernel_devices
tools.description: List all devices registered under a specific kernel, including adapter configs and device types.

tools.name: get_kernel_jobs
tools.description: List all jobs submitted to a specific kernel, including job status and progress.

tools.name: create_kernel
tools.description: Register a new Shop Kernel (physical site) on the PCC network. Part of Step 2 in the onboarding flow.

description.description: Description of the site and its capabilities

location.description: Location object with address and geo coordinates

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: List all jobs with status. Optionally filter by kernelId or status.

status.description: Filter by status (pending, queued, in_progress, paused, completed, failed, cancelled)

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Get job details including progress, evidence bundles, and milestones.

tools.name: update_job_status
tools.description: Update a job's status and optional progress percentage. Used by kernels to report job progress.

status.description: New status (pending, queued, in_progress, paused, completed, failed, cancelled). 'running' is accepted as a legacy alias for in_progress.

tools.name: list_escrows
tools.description: List escrow contracts with their milestone counts. Optionally filter by escrow status.

tools.name: get_escrow
tools.description: Get escrow details. Pass a DB ID for database record (with milestones and disputes), or an EVM address (0x...) to read directly from the blockchain.

escrowId.description: DB escrow ID or on-chain contract address (0x...)

tools.name: get_escrow_chain_state
tools.description: Read full on-chain escrow state with all milestone details from the blockchain. More detailed than get_escrow for on-chain contracts.

tools.name: get_escrow_events
tools.description: Get on-chain event history for an escrow contract. Returns funding, release, dispute, and bond events.

tools.name: get_token_balance
tools.description: Read an ERC-20 token balance for an account address from the blockchain.

account.description: Account address to check balance for (0x...)

tools.name: get_token_allowance
tools.description: Read the ERC-20 token allowance granted by an owner to a spender from the blockchain.

tools.name: get_escrow_dispute
tools.description: Read dispute state for a specific milestone from the blockchain.

tools.name: get_write_status
tools.description: Check if on-chain write operations are enabled (requires PCC_GATEWAY_PRIVATE_KEY to be configured). Returns write status and signer address.

tools.name: archive_evidence
tools.description: Archive an evidence bundle to IPFS/Storacha for permanent decentralized storage. Returns the content-addressed CID.

tools.name: get_evidence_bundle
tools.description: Get an encrypted evidence bundle by its bundle ID. Returns the encrypted payload and key capsules.

tools.name: grant_evidence_access
tools.description: Grant a new recipient access to an encrypted evidence bundle. Creates a re-encrypted key capsule for the recipient.

accessLevel.description: Level of access to grant (default: full)

tools.name: list_evidence_grants

tools.name: archive_encrypted_bundle

tools.name: get_bundle_ipfs
tools.description: Get IPFS CIDs for a bundle — returns the primary CID, metadata CID, and Filecoin deal ID if available.

tools.name: retrieve_ipfs
tools.description: Retrieve raw data from IPFS by CID. Used to fetch archived evidence bundles from decentralized storage.

tools.name: get_lit_conditions
tools.description: Get Lit Protocol access conditions for a Lit-encrypted evidence bundle. Returns the conditions that gate decryption.

tools.name: lit_decrypt
tools.description: Decrypt a Lit Protocol-encrypted evidence bundle using a Lit auth signature. Returns the decrypted bundle payload.

authSig.description: Lit auth signature object with sig, derivedVia, signedMessage, and address fields

tools.name: verify_evidence_zk
tools.description: Verify a ZK proof by its proof ID. Checks the proof against its verification key and public inputs.

proofId.description: ID of the ZK proof to verify

tools.name: commit_evidence

bundleHash.description: SHA-256 hash of the evidence bundle

tools.name: get_telemetry_stats
tools.description: Get aggregate pipeline telemetry statistics including phase timings, success rates, and throughput metrics across all jobs.

tools.name: get_active_telemetry
tools.description: List currently active jobs with their current pipeline phase and telemetry status.

tools.name: get_job_telemetry

jobId.description: Job ID to get pipeline timeline for

tools.name: get_telemetry_logs
tools.description: Query structured logs with filters for level, source, jobId, kernelId, time range, and full-text search.

after.description: Return logs after this ISO timestamp

before.description: Return logs before this ISO timestamp

tools.name: emit_telemetry
tools.description: Manually emit a telemetry event for a job pipeline phase. Used by kernels and agents to report execution progress.

phase.description: Pipeline phase name (e.g. intake, binding, execution, evidence, settlement)

tools.name: submit_for_human_verification
tools.description: Submit an evidence bundle for human verification. Selects a panel of verifiers from the network and returns assigned verifier IDs.

bundleHash.description: SHA-256 hash of the evidence bundle

photoRef.description: Reference to the photo evidence (CID or URL)

tools.name: get_verification_assignments
tools.description: Get pending verification assignments for a verifier node. Returns requests this verifier has been assigned but not yet responded to.

tools.name: get_verification_status
tools.description: Get verification status for a request. Returns vote tally, consensus state, dispute list, and pending response count.

tools.name: respond_to_verification
tools.description: Submit a verifier's verdict for a verification request. Returns consensus state after this vote.

tools.name: dispute_verification

disputerId.description: Verifier node ID filing the dispute

tools.name: register_capability_ip
tools.description: Record a capability as an IP asset. Story Protocol (now The DATA Foundation). These tools make no on-chain call: nothing is registered, claimed or disputed on chain. Any ipId, NFT token id or transaction hash in the reply is a placeholder, and no royalty is paid.

designerAddress.description: EVM address of the capability designer

commercialRevShare.description: Revenue share percentage for commercial use (0-100)

ipfsCid.description: IPFS CID of the capability spec document (optional)

tools.name: register_job_evidence_ip
tools.description: Record job evidence as a derivative of a capability's IP asset. Story Protocol (now The DATA Foundation). These tools make no on-chain call: nothing is registered, claimed or disputed on chain. Any id or transaction hash in the reply is a placeholder, and no royalty is paid.

parentIpId.description: IP ID of the parent capability

jobId.description: Job ID whose evidence is being registered

ipfsCid.description: IPFS CID of the evidence bundle (optional)

tools.name: distribute_royalties
tools.description: Set revenue splits for an IP asset among stakeholders (designer, operator, verifier, assembler, curator). Splits must sum to 100. Story Protocol (now The DATA Foundation). These tools make no on-chain call: nothing is registered, claimed or disputed on chain. No revenue is paid from these splits.

tools.name: pay_ip_royalty
tools.description: Record a royalty payment to an IP asset. Story Protocol (now The DATA Foundation). These tools make no on-chain call: nothing is registered, claimed or disputed on chain. No tokens move, and any transaction hash in the reply is a placeholder.

amount.description: Amount to pay in wei (as string)

tools.name: claim_ip_revenue
tools.description: Claim an IP asset's recorded revenue. Story Protocol (now The DATA Foundation). These tools make no on-chain call: nothing is registered, claimed or disputed on chain. Nothing is paid out: any amount or transaction hash in the reply is a placeholder.

tokenIds.description: Specific royalty token IDs to claim (optional — claims all if omitted)

tools.name: get_ip_revenue
tools.description: Get the revenue PCC has recorded for an IP asset. Story Protocol (now The DATA Foundation). These tools make no on-chain call: nothing is registered, claimed or disputed on chain. No revenue has been paid: any figure in the reply is a placeholder.

tools.name: get_ip_lineage
tools.description: Get the IP lineage PCC has recorded for an asset: parent capabilities and derivative job records. Story Protocol (now The DATA Foundation). These tools make no on-chain call: nothing is registered, claimed or disputed on chain.

tools.name: get_capability_ip
tools.description: Get the IP record PCC holds for a capability by its capability ID. Story Protocol (now The DATA Foundation). These tools make no on-chain call: nothing is registered, claimed or disputed on chain. Any id or transaction hash in it is a placeholder.

capabilityId.description: Capability ID to look up IP registration for

tools.name: raise_ip_dispute
tools.description: Record an IP dispute against an asset. Provide evidence hash and reason. Story Protocol (now The DATA Foundation). These tools make no on-chain call: nothing is registered, claimed or disputed on chain.

Returns supported chains (near, eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon), supported assets (USDC, USDT, NEAR, ETH, WBTC), and capability flags. Use this to confirm cross-chain settlement is available before requesting quotes.

amount.description: Amount as an integer string in the smallest denomination (e.g. '1000000' for 1 USDC with 6 decimals)

recipient.description: Recipient address on the destination chain (optional)

tools.name: near_intent
tools.description: Submit a cross-chain payment intent to the NEAR 1Click solver network. Creates a signed intent that routes the payment atomically across chains. Call near_quote first to obtain a quoteId. Intents typically settle within 30-60 seconds — poll near_intent_status to track progress.

workflowId.description: PCC workflow or job ID this payment is for

recipient.description: Recipient address on the destination chain (optional)

tools.name: near_intent_status
tools.description: Check the settlement status of a submitted NEAR 1Click cross-chain payment intent. Statuses progress: pending → submitted → settled | failed. Returns txHash and explorerUrl when settled.

tools.name: protocol_state
tools.description: Read the PCCProtocol root contract state: total escrow count and registry addresses. Requires PCC_PROTOCOL_ADDRESS to be configured on the gateway.

tools.name: pcc_dht_metrics
tools.description: Get a snapshot of DHT telemetry counters and recent events. Returns message counts, peer connection stats, query/announce rates, and a list of the last 50 metric events. Use for monitoring network health.

tools.name: system_telemetry
tools.description: Raw system state dump — actual DB rows for kernels, devices, jobs, evidence, registrations, capabilities, agent conversations, audit log. No fake numbers, no summaries.

tools.name: operator_poll_jobs
tools.description: Operator polls jobs assigned to their kernel; status defaults to queued, and the route can filter any status. Requires operate authority for this kernel: its recorded operator identity (the caller that registered it), its proven operator wallet, or the gateway admin authority. Another identity gets 403; no credentials gets 401; an unregistered kernel gets 404 for a non-admin. Operator identity proof for operate is completed by WP-A (DECISIONS items 136 and 138). The pcc-node daemon does not call it: it takes no jobs.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to poll jobs for

tools.name: operator_push_evidence
tools.description: Operator pushes evidence bundle from a completed job execution. Requires decide authority for the stored job's kernel: its proven operator wallet or the gateway admin authority. A matching claimed operator key gets 403 operator_proof_required. Evidence takes decide, per DECISIONS 2026-10-04 01:25 (N31c). Evidence is posted with the kernel's proven operator wallet authority (decide). The body's kernelId cannot choose the authorization target. No credentials gets 401 before the job read; a job without a kernel gets 403 for a non-admin. Contains device ID, execution timestamp, result payload, and event timeline. Success is a receipt with stored: true naming this jobId. HTTP 200 with stored: false means nothing was stored: never follow it with status completed.

tools.name: operator_heartbeat
tools.description: Operator sends heartbeat with capability re-announcement. Keeps the kernel alive on the network and updates its own capability rows. Requires operate authority for this kernel: its recorded operator identity (the caller that registered it), its proven operator wallet, or the gateway admin authority. Another identity gets 403; no credentials gets 401; an unregistered kernel gets 404 for a non-admin. Operator identity proof for operate is completed by WP-A (DECISIONS items 136 and 138).

tools.name: operator_update_job_status
tools.description: Operator reports a job's status (in_progress, completed, failed). Requires operate authority for the stored job's kernel: its recorded operator identity (the caller that registered it), its proven operator wallet, or the gateway admin authority. The body's kernelId cannot choose the authorization target. Another identity gets 403; no credentials gets 401 before the job read; a job without a kernel gets 403 for a non-admin. Operator identity proof for operate is completed by WP-A (DECISIONS items 136 and 138). The node path finishes a job in two calls: submit its evidence (POST /api/operator/evidence, posted with the kernel's proven operator wallet authority, decide), and only if that receipt says stored: true for this jobId, set status completed here. HTTP 200 alone is not enough: the relay answers 200 with stored: false when it could not store the evidence (an unknown job, a storage failure); then set failed with the reason evidence_not_stored. On the current gateway, completed marks the job done and its timeline then says settled, but the escrow is not released yet (board G1). Do not call pcc_job_complete after this: it answers 409.

tools.name: pcc_submit_paid_job
tools.description: Fast-track paid job: one call from DHT discovery to funded escrow + active scope. Auto-negotiates, quotes, creates escrow with milestones, creates execution scope. Returns jobId, scopeId, escrowId, quote with pricing adjustments, contract terms. For testnet, escrow is mock-funded automatically.

tools.name: pcc_job_complete
tools.description: Complete a job: gathers tool call audit trail from execution scopes, builds evidence bundle with SHA-256 hash, stores evidence, revokes scopes, and settles escrow (mock or real). This is how a job run through execution scopes is finished. A node that submitted its evidence and set status completed (operator_update_job_status) must not call it: it then answers 409 ("Job already completed or completion in progress"). Only the job's buyer, its kernel's operator or the gateway admin may call it: a buyer or operator must send an API key or session key in the Authorization header (a sign-in cookie alone gets 403), and any other proven wallet gets 404 ("Job not found").

tools.name: pcc_job_settlement
tools.description: Get a job's settlement status from its own escrow records: status (settled only when a settlement read confirms the release; reported_released when the milestone record says released but nothing confirms it; simulated for a mock escrow; awaiting_settlement, no_settlement_record, unknown or unavailable otherwise), settled, payout, paidAmount (confirmed releases only), reportedReleasedAmount, quotedAmount, currency (recorded or null), escrow, milestones, the negotiation session, notices and asOf.

tools.name: pcc_submit_request
tools.description: Submit a high-level capability request in natural language. The system automatically decomposes it into a capability DAG with dependencies, timelines, and budget allocation across fabrication, design, assembly, electronics, software, logistics, and verification nodes. Returns the request with full decomposed DAG. Example: 'Build a cute animatronic plush desk robot with servo-driven animations'.

description.description: Full natural language description of what needs to be built or done

urgency.description: Urgency level — affects cost multipliers (emergency: 2x cost, 0.5x time)

tools.name: pcc_list_requests
tools.description: List all capability requests with optional filtering. Shows status, decomposed DAG summary, estimated costs, and timelines.

tools.name: pcc_get_request
tools.description: Get a capability request by ID with the full decomposed DAG — all capability nodes, their dependencies, estimated costs/hours, assigned operators, and linked bounty IDs.

tools.name: pcc_decompose_request
tools.description: Re-trigger decomposition of an existing capability request. Overwrites the existing capability DAG with a fresh decomposition. Useful after updating the description or budget.

tools.name: pcc_publish_request
tools.description: Publish all pending capability nodes in a request as bounties. Each node becomes a bidding opportunity for operators. Returns the list of created bounty IDs linked to each capability node.

tools.name: pcc_get_request_dag
tools.description: Get the capability DAG (directed acyclic graph) for a request as adjacency data — nodes with all fields plus explicit edges showing dependency relationships. Useful for visualization or workflow planning.

tools.name: pcc_get_request_critical_path
tools.description: Get the critical path (longest dependency chain) for a capability request. The critical path determines the minimum calendar time to complete the request. Returns node IDs in order, the full node details, and total hours on the critical path.

tools.name: pcc_assign_node_operator
tools.description: Assign an operator to a specific capability node within a request. The node status changes to 'assigned'. Operators claim nodes to indicate they will execute that capability.

operatorId.description: Operator kernel ID or wallet address

tools.name: pcc_update_node_status
tools.description: Update the status of a capability node within a request. Valid transitions: pending → bidding → assigned → in_progress → completed (or failed). When all nodes complete, the request automatically moves to completed.

tools.name: pcc_update_request
tools.description: Update a capability request's title, description, budget, deadline, urgency, or contact info. Does not re-decompose — call pcc_decompose_request afterwards if you want a fresh DAG.

tools.name: pcc_cancel_request
tools.description: Cancel a capability request. Cancelled requests cannot be updated, decomposed, or published. This is a soft delete — the request remains visible with status 'cancelled'.

tools.name: pcc_oracle_status
tools.description: Not served by the PCC gateway: GET /api/oracle/health returns 404 there. PCC's verification oracle runs as a separate service, and this route answers only where a deployment fronts it. Agents never call the oracle to settle a job: settlement is the gateway's step after pcc_job_complete. Where it is served, it returns the oracle's EIP-712 signing address and chain ID.

tools.name: pcc_oracle_verify
tools.description: Not served by the PCC gateway: POST /api/oracle/verify returns 404 there. PCC's verification oracle runs as a separate service, and this route answers only where a deployment fronts it. Agents never call it to settle a job: settlement is the gateway's step after pcc_job_complete. Where it is served, it checks that the evidence exists, its hash matches, tier requirements are met, there is no replay and the operator identity is valid, and it returns a signed EIP-712 attestation.

tools.name: create_capability
tools.description: Register a capability instance for a kernel. Required before submitting jobs — the gateway needs at least one capability per kernel. Creates a liquid-handler, fdm, cnc-3axis, or other capability type.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to register capability for

type.description: Capability type (e.g. liquid-handler, fdm, cnc-3axis, laser-cut, document-printing)

description.description: Description of what this capability does

tools.name: kernel_heartbeat
tools.description: Send a per-kernel heartbeat to keep the kernel marked online. Used by pcc-node daemons as an alternative to the operator relay heartbeat.

tools.name: kernel_announce_capabilities
tools.description: Announce capabilities for a kernel. NOTE: the gateway currently acknowledges this call but stores nothing, so it does not put any capability on the network. To publish a capability, use create_capability (POST /api/capabilities).

devices.description: Device IDs that back these capabilities

tools.name: send_diagnostics
tools.description: Upload an encrypted diagnostic bundle when the operator's node has problems. The bundle is encrypted client-side with a retrieval code the operator must share with support before logs can be read. Use this when the operator reports errors, crashes, or misbehavior. The pcc-node CLI runs `pcc-node logs --send` locally to collect+encrypt; prefer that path when available. This tool is for agent-driven uploads when the bundle is already prepared.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID the diagnostics came from

bundleSize.description: Size of encrypted payload in bytes

logLineCount.description: How many log lines are in the bundle

collectedAt.description: ISO timestamp when bundle was collected

tools.name: send_support_message
tools.description: Send an operator support message to the PCC team. Creates a new support thread or appends to the operator's existing open thread. Can optionally attach a diagnostic retrieval code (from send_diagnostics) so support staff can decrypt logs. Discord webhook fires on every new message, so expect fast response. Use this whenever the operator says something is broken, confusing, or not behaving as expected.

message.description: The support message text — describe the problem concretely

subject.description: Optional thread subject (auto-generated from message if omitted)

retrievalCode.description: Optional diagnostic retrieval code to attach (from send_diagnostics)

systemInfo.description: Optional system context (platform, nodeVersion, daemonRunning, gatewayReachable)

tools.name: check_support_replies
tools.description: Check for admin replies on the operator's support threads. Call this periodically or when the operator asks 'did they respond yet?'. Returns all threads for this kernel and a hasUnreadReplies boolean indicating new admin messages.

tools.name: reply_to_support_thread
tools.description: Reply to an existing support thread. Use when the operator wants to add information to a thread started earlier. Needs the threadId from check_support_replies or the original send_support_message response.

retrievalCode.description: Optional diagnostic retrieval code to attach

tools.name: pcc_capture_challenge
tools.description: Issue a fresh block-anchored CaptureNonceChallenge for a job. The operator's device must render this nonce into the captured media (QR code, audio tone, etc.) before calling pcc_capture_upload. The nonce is derived from (challengeId, latest blockHash, workOutputRoot) so captures cannot be pre-computed. Returns challengeId, 64-char hex nonce, blockNumber, maxAgeSeconds (clamped to 120).

jobId.description: PCC job ID the capture belongs to

declaredClass.description: Capture class the operator plans to claim. Determines which gates the verifier will run.

requestedTtlSeconds.description: Requested challenge lifetime in seconds. Clamped to 120 server-side.

tools.name: pcc_capture_upload
tools.description: Upload a capture (photo / video / audio / sensor clip) with its CaptureManifest for G1..G6 verification. Bytes are base64-encoded inline; optional base64 C2PA manifest bytes can be supplied for CC3+ claims. The server runs the 6-gate CaptureVerifier and persists a PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL verdict. Returns {verdictId, verdict, verifiedClass, gatesPassed, gatesFailed, warnings, anchorCandidate, captureHash, manifestHash}.

manifest.description: CaptureManifest — ALCOA+-ready metadata: class, declaredAt (ISO-8601), deviceFingerprint, mediaHash (sha256:<hex>), optional challengeId. See CaptureManifestSchema in @pcc/spec.

captureBytesBase64.description: Base64-encoded capture bytes (image / video / audio / sensor clip). Hash must match manifest.mediaHash.

c2paManifestBase64.description: Optional base64-encoded C2PA manifest JUMBF bytes. Required when manifest.class >= CC3.

jobId.description: Job ID for telemetry binding. Falls back to manifest.jobId if omitted.

operatorId.description: Explicit operator ID. Falls back to the authenticated session userId.

challengeId.description: Challenge UUID to re-bind to the in-memory challenge cache (G3 freshness gate).

visualNonceEcho.description: The visual nonce value the operator rendered in-scene (QR payload, audio tone id, etc.).

submittedAt.description: Client-submitted timestamp (epoch ms). Used in drift detection.

tools.name: pcc_capture_anchor
tools.description: Anchor a PASS + anchor-candidate capture verdict to CaptureClassRegistry on-chain (Base Sepolia by default). Rejects FAIL/PARTIAL verdicts. Idempotent — re-submitting the same verdictId returns the existing anchor row. Returns 202 {status:'deferred'} if CaptureClassRegistry is not yet deployed (CAPTURE_REGISTRY_ADDRESS unset).

verdictId.description: The verdictId returned by pcc_capture_upload. Must be a PASS verdict with anchorCandidate=true.

tools.name: pcc_capture_status
tools.description: Fetch the combined verdict + on-chain anchor view for a single capture. Mirrors the verifier's DB shape plus the anchor tx metadata (txHash, blockNumber, gasUsed, explorerUrl). Anchor is null if the verdict was never anchored.

tools.name: pcc_list_verdicts
tools.description: List recent capture verdicts, newest first. Optionally filter by jobId. Default limit is 50, capped at 200 server-side. Returns {verdicts, count, limit, jobId}.

jobId.description: Filter by job ID. Omit for all verdicts across jobs.

tools.name: pcc_capture_class_registry
tools.description: Look up a capture's on-chain anchor record in CaptureClassRegistry by its 32-byte captureHash. Returns the registry address, captureHash, and decoded anchor tuple (declaredClass, verifiedClass, manifestHash, submittedBy, jobId, challengeId, blockAnchor, capturedAt, attestationsRoot, attesterCount). onchain is null if the capture was never anchored. Returns 202 deferred when CaptureClassRegistry is not yet deployed.

captureHash.description: Capture hash (32-byte). Accepts 0x-prefixed or unprefixed hex, or sha256:<hex> format. Padded server-side to bytes32.

tools.name: pcc_verifier_health
tools.description: Report CaptureVerifier health: which adapters are loaded (c2pa, webauthn, appattest, playintegrity), their staleness status, in-memory challenge cache size, whether CaptureClassRegistry is deployed, and the active PCC_NETWORK. Use this to diagnose why a capture class is being rejected or degraded.

tools.name: pcc_orchestrator_list_templates
tools.description: List the orchestrator templates the dashboard's chat console can drive. Each entry includes slug, display_name, description, produces_kind, capability_class (physical | digital), greeting, and api_base (the route prefix that serves the six session-driver routes for that template). Public — no auth required.

tools.name: pcc_orchestrator_match_capabilities
tools.description: Heuristic template matcher. Pass a free-text description of what you want to onboard (e.g. 'I run a CNC milling shop' or 'I have a Postgres database with a GraphQL endpoint') and the matcher returns all templates ranked by keyword score with a 'reason' string per match. Public — no auth required.

input.description: Free-text description of what you want to onboard.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_start
tools.description: Start a new physical-operator onboarding session. Returns a session_id used by every subsequent /api/onboard/* call. Auth-required.

url.description: Optional company website. If supplied, the orchestrator scrapes it on the next /scrape call.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_scrape
tools.description: Scrape a URL into the running physical-operator onboarding session. Triggers a stealth fetch + structured extraction (machines, hours, services, certifications). Returns a small JSON summary; full extraction is appended to the session's running profile and visible via /live-data. Auth-required.

url.description: URL to scrape (e.g. company About page).

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_ingest_docs
tools.description: Queue documents (datasheets, SOPs, MOPs, certifications) for ingestion into a physical-operator onboarding session. Document URLs may be local:// for files dropped in the chat console or full https:// URLs. Auth-required.

doc_urls.description: URLs of documents to ingest. Mix of local:// and https:// is fine.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_build_agent
tools.description: Finalise a physical-operator onboarding session. It mints no wallet, and it can't register the operator yet: its register call sends no API key, so the gateway refuses it and this call answers 500 `build_failed` with the refusal in `message`. A retry repeats the same refused call. Auth-required.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_status
tools.description: Coarse status snapshot for a physical-operator onboarding session: current state, 0-100 progress, scraped_count, ingested_count, last_event, publication payload (if built). Cheap — designed for polling from the chat header. Auth-required.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_live_data
tools.description: Full event log for a physical-operator onboarding session — feeds the chat console's activity sidebar. Supports incremental polling via ?since=<unix-millis>. Returns the next cursor on every response. Auth-required.

since.description: Unix milliseconds cursor — returns only events with t > since. Use the 'cursor' field of the previous response for incremental polling.

tools.name: pcc_contributor_register
tools.description: Register a contributor profile binding a wallet address to a role and a published RateSchedule. Body: address (0x40hex), role (10 ContributorRole values from ADR-12 §2.1 + legacy 'designer'), scheduleHash (0x64hex of a previously published schedule), optional ipId, metadataUri, contributorNftTokenId. Returns the persisted profile (composite id is address:role:tail). Idempotent on the composite id — re-posting the same (address, role, contributorNftTokenId) replaces the prior profile.

scheduleHash.description: 0x + 64 hex sha256 of a published RateSchedule

ipId.description: Optional Story Protocol IP Asset ID

contributorNftTokenId.description: Optional ContributorNFT tokenId once minted on-chain

tools.name: pcc_contributor_list
tools.description: List all contributor profiles for an address across roles. Returns an array of {id, address, role, scheduleHash, ipId, contributorNftTokenId, metadataUri, registeredAt}. Returns empty array when no profiles exist for the address.

tools.name: pcc_schedule_publish
tools.description: Publish a sealed off-chain RateSchedule. Computes scheduleHash server-side via the canonical sha256-over-canonical-JSON algorithm (matching the on-chain RateScheduleRegistry.publish() invariant). Idempotent: re-publishing the same content returns alreadyPublished:true. Returns {scheduleHash, alreadyPublished}.

schedule.description: RateSchedule body — version, segments (constant/step/linear-decay/exponential-decay/adoption-indexed/piecewise-value), and optional notes

tools.name: pcc_schedule_get
tools.description: Fetch a published RateSchedule by its content hash. Returns {schedule, publishedBy} with segments re-validated via Zod, or 404 if not found.

tools.name: pcc_schedule_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate a published RateSchedule at a moment, returning the effective bps. Inputs: scheduleHash + now (unix seconds) + optional jobValueCents (piecewise-value) + optional jobsPerDay (adoption-indexed). Returns {scheduleHash, bps, segmentKind, segmentIndex}. segmentIndex=-1 + bps=0 when no segment covers the moment (silent gap).

tools.name: pcc_training_manifest_set
tools.description: Set (insert-or-replace) the TrainingManifest for a model IP — the dataset weight map the LicensingEngine walks when distributing payouts to a 'model-author' entry in a CompositionManifest. Dataset weightBps must sum to ≤ 10000 (gateway accepts partial mixes; on-chain enforces exact 10000). Returns {modelIpId, manifestHash}.

modelIpId.description: Story IP Asset ID for the model

baseModelIpId.description: Optional parent ModelNFT IP if this was fine-tuned

tools.name: pcc_training_manifest_get
tools.description: Fetch the TrainingManifest for a model IP. Returns the parsed datasets array + manifestHash + createdAt, or 404 if no manifest has been set.

modelIpId.description: Story IP Asset ID for the model

tools.name: attach_operator_channel
tools.description: Attach a notification/dispatch channel to an operator so PCC knows how to ping them when a job lands. The operator's onboarding agent calls this AFTER the conversation that produced the channel record. Transport is a small stable enum (webhook|email|sms|voice|push|mqtt|file|manual) — vendor specifics live in the free-form `describe` field, written by the operator's agent. PCC the substrate stays neutral. Returns the channel record with a generated id.

slug.description: Operator slug (typically the operator's address or unique identifier).

label.description: Short human label shown to the operator and in admin UIs: 'Front counter printer', 'Owner's phone'.

transport.description: Which wire does the message go over. `manual` = no machine endpoint (dashboard-only).

direction.description: out=PCC pushes only; in-out=operator's system also replies; in=operator pushes unsolicited.

endpoint.description: Transport-specific routing payload. webhook→{url}, email→{address}, sms/voice→{phoneE164}, push→{token,platform}, mqtt→{brokerUrl,topic}, file→{scheme,path}, manual→{}.

credentialRef.description: Reference to a secret in the credential vault (not the secret itself). PCC resolves it at dispatch time.

describe.description: Plain-English instructions for how PCC should talk to whatever is on the other end. Written by the operator's onboarding agent. Required, ≥4 chars. Example: 'POST JSON with keys order_id, line_items[], deadline_iso. I will POST back {order_id, status} to your reply URL.'

replyContract.description: Optional operator-authored contract describing how the operator's system will respond to evidence requests, status pings, etc.

enabled.description: Whether the channel is live (defaults to true).

tools.name: list_operator_channels
tools.description: List every channel attached to an operator. Returns the full channel records (id, transport, direction, endpoint, describe, enabled flags). Useful for an operator's onboarding agent to confirm what is wired up, and for status dashboards.

tools.name: update_operator_channel
tools.description: Update an existing channel — toggle enabled, rewrite the describe contract, change the endpoint payload, etc. Merges into the existing record. The operator slug, id, and createdAt are immutable.

tools.name: delete_operator_channel
tools.description: Remove a channel from an operator. Future jobs will not dispatch to it. Use update_operator_channel with enabled=false to silence temporarily without losing the recipe in `describe`.

tools.name: test_operator_channels
tools.description: Fire a synthetic job at every enabled channel for an operator so the onboarding agent (and the human watching) can confirm the integration end-to-end before a real job lands. Returns per-channel dispatch results (delivered, ref, warnings).

tools.name: suggest_csd_templates
tools.description: Bidirectional onboarding: the registry talks back. Describe in plain English what you are trying to set up — 'wood-fired pizza shop in SF', 'Opentrons OT-2 liquid handler', 'same-day SF courier' — and the registry returns N candidate Capability StructureDefinition (CSD) templates ranked by keyword-overlap relevance (name×3, tags×2, description×1; tie-break on usage). Empty query falls back to popularity-ordered top picks. After picking one, pass the chosen type to pcc-author-integration. Score-zero results are dropped.

q.description: Plain-English description of the capability the user is trying to set up. Optional — empty falls back to popularity.

tools.name: get_popular_csd_templates
tools.description: Return CSDs sorted by adoption (usage-count descending). Useful for first-time operators who want to see what kind of capabilities others are publishing. Each entry includes the CSD record plus usage attribution: count, recent adopters (deduped, capped at 50), and lastUsedAt.

tools.name: get_operator_status
tools.description: Four-slot substrate view for an operator: kernels, capabilities (with sla + availability), notification channels, and the per-kernel A2A agent-card URLs. Returns totals and a `missing` list naming any of the four onboarding slots that are still empty. Use this from an onboarding agent's wrap-up step to confirm 'are all four slots wired before I go live?' status is `ready` | `partial` | `unconfigured`. Public — operator slug is non-secret and the response carries no credentials (channel `credentialRef` values are vault references, not secrets).

slug.description: Operator slug — typically the operator's wallet address used as `operatorAddress` on their kernels.

tools.name: propose_composition
tools.description: Propose a composition — a sequenced DAG of capability instances to satisfy a multi-step outcome under a budget + assurance tier. Accepts either a flat `steps` list or an outcome chain. Returns a candidate plan ranked by `optimizeFor` (price | speed | quality) with per-step assignments. The composition is persisted for ~30 minutes (proposed status) and can be executed once via execute_composition.

steps.description: Ordered list of capability types this composition needs (1..20). Use this OR `outcomeChain`.

outcomeChain.description: Alternative to `steps`: a chain of named sub-outcomes. The planner uses only the last entry, as the outcome type to plan for.

budgetUSD.description: Total budget the user is willing to spend across all steps.

minAssuranceTier.description: Minimum acceptable assurance tier on every step.

location.description: Geographic constraint: lat and lng (both required) and an optional radiusKm.

requester.description: {agentId, did?} — the agent submitting the request.

tools.name: get_composition
tools.description: Retrieve a previously-proposed composition by id. Returns 404 if unknown, 410 if the 30-minute proposal window has expired. Use this to inspect a plan before executing, or to recover a plan id after a restart.

tools.name: execute_composition
tools.description: Commit a proposed composition: drives the DAG through the workflow engine, each step records a reputation outcome, the composition's reputation is finalized when the run ends. When `PCC_COMPOSE_EXECUTE_REAL=true` is set on the gateway, steps submit real jobs via JobFacade and the workflow run is durable (@pcc/workflow). When the flag is off, the NOOP runner returns synthetic success — useful in dev/test. Re-executing an already-run composition replays the stored result (idempotent — reputation deltas are applied exactly once).

id.description: Composition id from propose_composition. Must be in `proposed` status and not expired.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional string, 1-120 characters. The gateway validates it but doesn't use it.

tools.name: pcc_report
tools.description: Report a bug, friction, or dead-end you hit while using PCC. Call this the moment you get stuck and cannot recover: a 5xx (its response carries a `report_hint` with pre-filled fields), a 4xx you cannot fix from its message, the same step failing twice, or a misleading tool/description. PUBLIC — works before you provision an API key (cold agents are exactly who this is for). Persisted durably and reviewed by the PCC team. Report each distinct failure ONCE; never include an API key, token, or wallet secret. Rate-limited per IP.

type.description: bug = something is broken/wrong; friction = it works but was confusing/harder than it should be; idea = a suggestion or missing capability. Defaults to bug.

summary.description: 1-line description of what you were doing and what went wrong. Example: 'POST /api/build/contract returned 500 with no hint about the missing field.'

detail.description: Multi-line context: the full error body, what you tried, what you expected. Optional but recommended.

endpoint.description: The route you were on when you got stuck. From a 5xx `report_hint.send.endpoint`. Example: '/api/build/contract'.

method.description: The HTTP method you used. From `report_hint.send.method`. Example: 'POST'.

status.description: The HTTP status you got. From `report_hint.send.status`. Example: 500.

errorCode.description: The machine error code from the response body, if any. From `report_hint.send.errorCode`.

traceId.description: Your journey ID — returned by provision_api_key and on every response as `x-pcc-trace-id` (also in a 5xx `report_hint.traceId`). Lets PCC replay your full run.

severity.description: How badly this blocked you. Optional.

agentId.description: Which model/agent you are. Example: 'claude', 'gpt-4o', 'gemini'. Optional.

logs.description: Optional but valuable: your last few steps as SUMMARIES (never full request/response bodies) — the sequence that led to the failure. Secrets are never allowed in a note.

note.description: One line on what happened at this step.

tools.name: pcc_report_attempt
tools.description: Report one phase of an onboarding attempt, success or failure (attempt reporting contract v1). Send one report when each runbook phase ends, and a final report with phase "session" (with the `phases` roll-up), also when you stop early (outcome abandoned or budget_stop). Generate `sessionId` (UUID v4) once per attempt and increment `seq` with every report; a retried report with the same sessionId and seq is collapsed. Never guess: send null for what you do not know (tokens: source "unknown"). Redact keys, tokens, emails and wallet secrets before sending. Always include `summary`: contract v1 makes it optional, but until the gateway's attempt support lands it is the only field kept, and today's server refuses a report without it. The schema is contract v1: an unknown phase, outcome or harness name is accepted (the server stores it as other or unknown, with the raw value as a label), and budget-stop is a spelling of budget_stop. Never send a transcript; consent.transcript stays false until the operator decides. Unauthenticated.

sessionId.description: UUID v4, generated once at the start of the attempt

anyOf.description: Any other value: the server stores "other", with the raw value (clamped to 64 characters) as phaseLabel.
Any other value: the server stores "unknown", with the raw value as outcomeLabel.

durationMs.description: The phase's wall time; on session, the whole attempt

logs.description: The phase's step timeline, summaries only

anyOf.description: Any other value: the server stores "other", with the raw value (clamped to 64 characters) as phaseLabel.
Any other value: the server stores "unknown", with the raw value as outcomeLabel.

ids.description: Only the ids known so far: each at most 200 characters of [A-Za-z0-9:._/-], or null

anyOf.description: Any other name: the server stores "other", with the raw name as label.

digest.description: sha256:<64 hex> of this package's bytes

tokens.description: Never guess: send null with source "unknown"

traceId.description: x-pcc-trace-id of the last PCC call

tools.name: save_dashboard
tools.description: Save a generated dashboard to the network so the user gets a live, shareable URL: https://capability.network/a/<slug>. Pass a `manifest` — a small declarative DashboardManifest (windows + live-data bindings + actions) conforming to the schema at https://capability.network/ui-kit/v1/manifest.schema.json; the shipped pcc-ui kit renders it identically everywhere (you compose the manifest, the kit renders it — never hand-rolled HTML). WHEN to call this: only when the task needs a surface to watch/approve/compare/reuse (a live job, a value chain, a settlement trail, a recurring order) — never for a one-line answer. RECALL FIRST: call search_dashboards before generating; reload or fork a match instead of duplicating. The manifest MUST NOT contain an API key (a shared artifact travels with its contents — the network rejects one that does). Returns the stored artifact incl. its slug. Defaults visibility to 'unlisted' (link-shareable, not listed).

name.description: Short human name for the dashboard, e.g. 'Watch my pizza + courier'. Used to mint the slug.

description.description: One-line description of what the dashboard shows.

manifest.description: The DashboardManifest (2-6KB JSON) conforming to https://capability.network/ui-kit/v1/manifest.schema.json. Required top-level keys: `csd` (must be 'pcc://artifacts/dashboard/v1'), `title`, and `sections[]` (each section has `windows[]`). Window kinds: note, metric, capability, list, form, run, approval, receipt, chain, actions. Bindings point at live routes you already use (/api/jobs/:id, /api/escrow/:id, /sse/stream/job/:id). No API key anywhere in the manifest.

capabilityTypes.description: Capability types this dashboard is about, e.g. ['pizza.order','courier.dispatch']. This is the discovery join — it's how search_dashboards finds this artifact later.

composeRefs.description: Optional pinned, re-plannable ComposeRequest objects (value chains). Pin the request, never a compositionId (those expire in 30 min).

visibility.description: Who can load it. Default 'unlisted' (anyone with the link; not in listings). 'public' appears in search_dashboards; 'private' is owner-only.

renderedCid.description: Optional CID of a rendered-HTML export saved via /api/storage.

tools.name: get_dashboard
tools.description: Recall a saved dashboard by its id or slug. Returns the full artifact (manifest + metadata). Use this to reload a dashboard the user asks for again ('open my pizza dashboard') instead of regenerating it — a saved dashboard reloads with zero regeneration. Public for public/unlisted artifacts; owner-only for private ones. Increments the load counter (a popularity signal).

idOrSlug.description: The artifact id (ua_...) or its slug (e.g. 'watch-my-pizza-8k3f', the tail of the /a/<slug> URL).

tools.name: search_dashboards
tools.description: Discover existing public dashboards before you generate a new one (recall-first — the library accrues; adopt > extend > build for UIs too). Filter by `capabilityType` (e.g. 'pizza.order'), free-text `q` over name/description/types, and `sort` by popularity or recency. Returns { entries, total, offset, limit }. Only public artifacts are listed; unlisted ones load by slug via get_dashboard but never appear here.

capabilityType.description: Filter to dashboards tagged with this capability type, e.g. 'pizza.order'.

q.description: Free-text search over name, description, and capability types.

tools.name: fork_dashboard
tools.description: Fork an existing dashboard into a new artifact you own, preserving lineage back to the original (the social remix verb). Use this to adapt a popular dashboard rather than build from scratch — e.g. fork a 'watch pizza' dashboard and raise the budget or add a receipt window via update_dashboard. Increments the source's fork counter. You can fork any public/unlisted artifact, or a private one you own.

id.description: The id (ua_...) of the artifact to fork.

name.description: Optional name for the fork (defaults to '<original> (fork)').

tools.name: update_dashboard
tools.description: Modify a dashboard you own (owner-only). Replace the manifest or any metadata field; the version increments. Use this to edit a saved surface meaningfully — 'raise budgetUSD to 40', 'add a receipt window', 'make it public'. A replaced manifest must still conform to the schema and must not contain an API key. Only send the fields you want to change.

id.description: The id (ua_...) of the artifact to update.

manifest.description: Replacement DashboardManifest (must conform to the schema; no API key). Omit to leave the manifest unchanged.

visibility.description: New visibility (e.g. flip 'unlisted' -> 'public' to list it).

tools.name: render_pcc_dashboard
tools.description: Compose a live PCC dashboard for a physical-capability task — pass a DashboardManifest (windows + live data bindings + actions) and it renders as an interactive MCP App.

inputSchema.title: PCC Dashboard Manifest
inputSchema.description: JSON-Schema mirror of @pcc/spec DashboardManifestSchema (packages/spec/src/types/ui-artifact.ts). The small declarative dashboard a person's LLM emits; the pcc-ui kit renders it. Windows are a closed set rendered textContent-only. Actions never carry confirm:"none" (a human click is the confirm step). A manifest must NOT contain an API key (pcc_live_/pcc_test_) anywhere — a shared artifact travels with its contents. This mirror now carries the Zod RESOURCE CAPS (sections/windows/actions maxItems 24, list.limit max 200, meta maxItems 12, pollMs minimum 2000) so a generator validating only against this schema does not emit manifests the gateway then rejects. TWO Zod guards are not expressible as JSON-Schema validation and are enforced only by the gateway's Zod (the authoritative gate): the 256KB byte cap (MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES) and the recursive no-credential refine (containsApiKey — rejects a baked pcc key / Bearer / JWT, raw, percent-encoded, or base64). Validate against the Zod DashboardManifestSchema for the full gate.

csd.description: The builtin CSD URI this manifest conforms to.

inputSchema.title: PCC Dashboard Manifest
inputSchema.description: JSON-Schema mirror of @pcc/spec DashboardManifestSchema (packages/spec/src/types/ui-artifact.ts). The small declarative dashboard a person's LLM emits; the pcc-ui kit renders it. Windows are a closed set rendered textContent-only. Actions never carry confirm:"none" (a human click is the confirm step). A manifest must NOT contain an API key (pcc_live_/pcc_test_) anywhere — a shared artifact travels with its contents. This mirror now carries the Zod RESOURCE CAPS (sections/windows/actions maxItems 24, list.limit max 200, meta maxItems 12, pollMs minimum 2000) so a generator validating only against this schema does not emit manifests the gateway then rejects. TWO Zod guards are not expressible as JSON-Schema validation and are enforced only by the gateway's Zod (the authoritative gate): the 256KB byte cap (MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES) and the recursive no-credential refine (containsApiKey — rejects a baked pcc key / Bearer / JWT, raw, percent-encoded, or base64). Validate against the Zod DashboardManifestSchema for the full gate.
